title: Agent specialization and task ownership
content: Specialization gives each agent a bounded responsibility and a clear result contract. The supervisor owns delegation and workflow progress; a research agent finds candidate sources; a RAG agent retrieves relevant local passages.

title: Shared state and agent communication
content: Shared state is the typed handoff between agents. Agents return results rather than silently changing workflow ownership. The supervisor records each result before selecting the next step.

title: Analysis, validation, and result aggregation
content: An analysis agent combines evidence and identifies themes. A validation agent checks that claims have sources and flags missing evidence. A writer aggregates the validated results into a concise final answer.

title: Multi-agent workflow limitations
content: Multi-agent systems add coordination overhead, latency, and more opportunities for failure. Shared state, bounded tasks, clear ownership, and validation improve observability but do not guarantee factual correctness.
